parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.part_stem:
A Hall probe containing a thin slice of semiconducting material is placed in a uniform magnetic field of flux density $B$. The largest faces of the slice are perpendicular to the magnetic field, as shown in Fig. 7.1.
{{figure:figure_7_1}}
Fig. 7.1
The thickness $x$ of the slice is $1.8\text{mm}$. The number density of charge carriers in the semiconducting material is $1.5 \times 10^{16}\text{m}^{-3}$.
A constant current of $5.4\text{A}$ is passed through the slice between the shaded faces.
The Hall voltage $V_{\text{H}}$ that is developed between the terminals PQ is recorded.
Fig. 7.2 shows the variation with time $t$ of $B$.
{{figure:figure_7_2}}
Fig. 7.2
parts.text: Show that, when $B$ is equal to $4.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{T}$, the magnitude of $V_{\text{H}}$ is $5.0\text{V}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
(b)(i)
parts.part_stem:
The Hall probe in (a) is replaced with a small flat coil that has 3000 turns. The cross-sectional area of the coil is $3.4 \times 10^{-4}\text{m}^{2}$.
The plane of the coil is perpendicular to the magnetic field. The electromotive force (e.m.f.) $E$ induced between the terminals of the coil is recorded as $B$ varies as shown in Fig. 7.2.
parts.text: Show that the magnitude of $E$ at time $t = 0.010\text{s}$ is $2.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{V}$.
